scope: Root v4 authoring, metadata, local learner workflow, publication and release guards against planning/overhaul_v4.md. This review author owns the separately reported firmware/integration labs; this is an independent review of root delivery tooling, not a second independent audit of those labs.

findings.problem: Adding the next function to a shared learner C source invalidated the prior unit prerequisite, obstructing the intended progression through the existing family scaffolds.
findings.resolution: Acceptance retains content-addressed source/evidence revisions. Historical prerequisite validity is distinct from live claims and export validity; altered unit contracts or damaged retained objects invalidate the history.
findings.validation: Reproduced the original failure in a disposable workflow fixture; the final same-source evolution regression passes and verifies that stale live exports remain blocked.

findings.problem: Combining an early monolithic provider export containing later stubs with a newer export could let static linking select a stale stub from the first archive.
findings.resolution: Verified component imports reject differing snapshots of the same source path within one adapter role and reject conflicting target identities. The workflow requires coherent re-exports or distinct source ownership.
findings.validation: The progressive stub-to-implementation regression rejects conflicting snapshots, then passes after explicit coherent re-export; actual P1 import checks use verified regenerated CMake targets.

findings.problem: A retained-family runner that exited before writing new receipts could have old v3 success records repinned as current before the wrapper raised.
findings.resolution: The wrapper writes pending/failed status, removes expected stale output names before launch, requires zero exit and newly emitted successful receipts, checks source identity stability, and restores historical bytes in finally.
findings.validation: Four isolated wrapper cases verify nonzero exit, missing new receipts, source mutation, and fresh successful receipt pinning with historical restoration.

findings.identified_by: Root final capstone scope audit; independently rereviewed here.
findings.problem: The final MCU portfolio retained earlier board/interface captures but did not require current integrated-application deployment, fault/recovery and perturbation observations explicitly required by CAP-MCU-02 through CAP-MCU-04. The integration stage sequence also needed explicit prior-stage dependencies.
findings.resolution: All three MCU final units now declare their own local F439 physical claim and manual capture registration, without source_units substitution. Their steps specify current integrated image/source and raw observations. Existing H745/F439 and ten-interface portfolio obligations remain. Every integration stage consumes its preceding final; CAP-LINUX-03 and CAP-MCU-03 retain the integration family workspace and explicit cross-family transitions preserve prior dossiers and source.
findings.validation: Canonical init and study-sheet generation passed for the three MCU finals. Each generated template requires a local physical claim and rejects an empty observation set. Advancing the actual CAP02 integration workspace into CAP03 preserved learner source bytes. check_v4 passed all ten negative controls, including missing deployment/recovery captures and portfolio substitution.

checks.assessment: Exact minute allocations preserve each original project envelope; new units replace work in those envelopes. Reading, review and consolidation categories reconcile without charging reuse twice.

Canonical unit inspection reports no errors. Prerequisite edges are ordered and explicit; the first bounded tool is reachable after 6 assigned hours and the real file boundary after 35, excluding diagnosis. Strand adaptation stays within 24 hours. Integration implementation milestones require sealed alternatives and later implementation/check evidence.

All 494 historical teaching/identity hashes match the v4 baseline. A git comparison against 4f3e3a2 shows no differences for original module/project teaching, taxonomies, program, project graph, migration_v3 or reference catalog. Receipt wrappers preserve historical results instead of relabeling them.

Registry producers, consumer prerequisites, import contracts and critical facets reconcile. Exports retain actual source/header/dependency closures; integration CMake consumes verified learner targets. Missing providers or missing all-tests coverage cannot become an assessor fallback or automatic success.

Recall starts only after explicit study, preserves original attempts and superseding grades, rotates topic variants, and scores objective facets. Early practice cannot compress spacing; failed or assisted work needs a later independent retry. Due queues are bounded, and contract-specific preflights retain their distinct evidence.

Shared-source evolution retains historical prerequisites; current claims and exports still become stale. Canonical manual interface capture targets make physical obligations recordable without inventing executable targets. Final portfolios require retained F439/H745 and all ten interface observations; SMP milestones require actual guest receipts for 1, 2 and 4 CPUs. Host/model/build evidence cannot close physical or emulator claims. CAP-MCU-02, CAP-MCU-03 and CAP-MCU-04 additionally require their own current integrated F439 observations; earlier component portfolios cannot discharge those local claims. Campaign stages preserve the existing integration workspace, and cross-family transitions are explicit.

Publication renders current working units before preserved historical briefs and validates cross-references. Acceptance requires current source-bound publication and pinned successful execution/review receipts, rejecting unresolved medium/high findings. Packaging stages four archives, excludes assessor paths from learner bundles, validates archived accepted bytes, rebuilds extracted source, compares HTML/Markdown, and checks input stability before rollback-capable promotion.
